proposals.before: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Public Lands and then transferred to serve concurrently as vice director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and vice director of the Right Office.
proposals.after: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Public Lands and then transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and vice director of the Right Office.
proposals.reason: Chinese 轉祠部、右司二員外 records paired transfers to two yuanwailang posts and does not say the two offices were held concurrently.

proposals.before: He authored 《Three Rites Illustrations》 in nine fascicles, 《Subtle Meanings of the Five Classics》 in fourteen fascicles, and 《Phonological Glosses on Mencius》 in three fascicles.
proposals.after: He authored Three Rites Illustrations in nine fascicles, Subtle Meanings of the Five Classics in fourteen fascicles, and Phonological Glosses on Mencius in three fascicles.
proposals.reason: English title translations are wrapped in Chinese book-title brackets, which fuses source punctuation into the translation.

proposals.before: He compiled 《Three Rites Illustrations》 in nine fascicles, 《Subtle Meanings of the Five Classics》 in fourteen fascicles, and 《Phonological Glosses on Mencius》 in three fascicles.
proposals.after: He compiled Three Rites Illustrations in nine fascicles, Subtle Meanings of the Five Classics in fourteen fascicles, and Phonological Glosses on Mencius in three fascicles.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise wraps translated titles in Chinese book-title brackets instead of rendering the titles in English.

proposals.before: Lu Qi resented Zhang Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to entrap him. As troops were then being deployed on the western frontier, Qi falsely offered to go in person. The emperor firmly refused, and instead recommended Zhang Yi, with the title of vice director of the Secretariat, as military governor of Fengxiang-Longyou to replace Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi then entered into an alliance with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.
proposals.after: Lu Qi resented Zhang Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to entrap him. As troops were then being deployed on the western frontier, Qi falsely offered to go in person. The emperor firmly refused, and Qi therefore recommended Zhang Yi, with the title of vice director of the Secretariat, as military governor of Fengxiang-Longyou to replace Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi then entered into an alliance with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.
proposals.reason: The subject of 因薦鎰 is Lu Qi, who recommended Zhang Yi after the emperor refused Qi's own offer; the idiomatic English wrongly makes the emperor the recommender.

proposals.before: At first it was agreed that Han would use an ox and Tibet a horse as sacrificial victims; Yi was ashamed to ally with them and, intending to diminish the rite, therefore requested of Jiezan, saying: 'Han cannot plow without oxen, and Tibet cannot travel without horses—now I request that sheep, pigs, and dogs be substituted for the three animals.'
proposals.after: At first it was agreed that Han would use an ox and Tibet a horse as sacrificial victims; Yi was ashamed to ally with them and, intending to diminish the rite, therefore requested of Jiezan, saying: 'Han cannot plow without oxen, and Tibet cannot travel without horses—now I request that the three animals sheep, pigs, and dogs be substituted for them.'
proposals.reason: 三物代之 means the sheep, pigs, and dogs are the three substitutes, not that they replace some other three animals.

proposals.before: When Zhang Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, his two sons were seized by scouting cavalry, and Li Chulin had them all killed;
proposals.after: When Zhang Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, he and his two sons were all seized by scouting cavalry, and Li Chulin killed them all;
proposals.reason: 及二子皆為候騎所得 and 俱殺之 include Zhang Yi with his two sons as those captured and killed, which the following posthumous honors confirm.

proposals.before: When Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, his two sons were both seized by scouting cavalry, and Chulin killed them all;
proposals.after: When Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, he and his two sons were all seized by scouting cavalry, and Chulin killed them all;
proposals.reason: The Chinese coordinates Yi with 二子 as joint objects of capture and of 俱殺之.

proposals.before: Lin Fu's son Xiangdao served as right chief minister at the beginning of the Longde era; Xiangdao was Congyi's great-great-uncle.
proposals.after: Lin Fu's son Xiangdao served as right chief minister at the beginning of the Linde era; Xiangdao was Congyi's great-granduncle.
proposals.reason: 麟德 is the Linde reign (AD 664-665), not Longde; 曾伯祖 is a great-grandfather brother (great-granduncle).

proposals.before: At first, Lin Fu begot Xiangdao, who in the beginning of Longde served as right chief minister; Xiangdao was Congyi's great-great-uncle.
proposals.after: At first, Lin Fu begot Xiangdao, who in the beginning of Linde served as right chief minister; Xiangdao was Congyi's great-granduncle.
proposals.reason: Same source errors: 麟德 romanized as Longde and 曾伯祖 as great-great-uncle.

proposals.before: Within several months, because of kinship avoidance he was removed and appointed vice director of the Bureau of Punishments.
proposals.after: Within several months, because of kinship avoidance he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Punishments.
proposals.reason: 除 here means to appoint, not to remove.

proposals.before: Fu replied, "I am selling my old estate because my family is poor, intending only to rescue widows and children. If I exchanged it for a fine post for myself and left those within my gates to freeze and starve, that would not be the heart of an honorable man."
proposals.after: Fu replied, "I am selling my old estate because my family is poor, intending only to rescue widows and children. If I exchanged it for a fine post for myself and left those within my gates to freeze and starve, that would not be the heart of a base man."
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄙夫 means a base or petty man; the idiomatic rendering inverts this into 'honorable man' and reverses Fu's self-deprecating refusal.

proposals.before: He later rose successively to director in the Secretariat.
proposals.after: He later rose successively to a director in the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書郎 is a lang of the Shangshu (Department of State Affairs), not the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: Later he successively rose to director in the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Later he successively rose to a director in the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: Same office error as the idiomatic line: 尚書郎 is not a Secretariat post.

proposals.before: During Zhide he served as staff judge to Jiangxi investigation commissioner Huangfu Shen and was successively removed and appointed military adjutant of Quzhou.
proposals.after: During Zhide he served as staff judge to Jiangxi investigation commissioner Huangfu Shen and was successively appointed military adjutant of Quzhou.
proposals.reason: 累除 means successive appointment; 除 is appoint, not remove.

proposals.before: Then he apologized, saying: 'But for you two gentlemen, I would nearly have become an old man's dim incompetence.'
proposals.after: Then he apologized, saying: 'But for you two gentlemen, I would nearly have become a dim and incompetent old man.'
proposals.reason: 暗劣 describes the speaker himself as dim and incompetent.

proposals.before: After two years, Cui Youfu entered the chief ministry and recommended him as remonstrance official and promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Zhejiang East and West. He was successively promoted to left vice director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: After two years, Cui Youfu entered the chief ministry and recommended him as remonstrance official and promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Zhejiang East and West. He was successively promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書左丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: When recovery was achieved, Hun's name was still listed. He submitted, saying, "Recently I was stained by the mad rebel. I am truly ashamed to use my old name. Moreover the character may carry the spear radical, and now is the time to rest arms. I request to change my name to Hun."
proposals.after: When recovery was achieved, Hun was still named Zai. He submitted, saying, "Recently I was stained by the mad rebel. I am truly ashamed to use my old name. Moreover the character may carry the spear radical, and now is the time to rest arms. I request to change my name to Hun."
proposals.reason: 尚名載 means he was still named Zai, not that a name remained listed.

proposals.before: When recovery was achieved, Hun's name was still listed; he thereupon submitted, saying: 'Recently I was stained by the mad rebel; your servant is truly ashamed to use the old name, moreover the character may carry the spear radical—now is the time to rest arms; I request to change my name to Hun.'
proposals.after: When recovery was achieved, Hun was still named Zai; he thereupon submitted, saying: 'Recently I was stained by the mad rebel; your servant is truly ashamed to use the old name, moreover the character may carry the spear radical—now is the time to rest arms; I request to change my name to Hun.'
proposals.reason: 尚名載 means still named Zai.

proposals.before: In the first month of the third year he was additionally made Associate Grand Councilor and continued to oversee the Secretariat.
proposals.after: In the first month of the third year he was additionally made Associate Grand Councilor and continued to oversee the Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 判門下省 is the Chancellery, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Moreover, it is spring, when executions are carried out. Allow me to itemize and memorialize the fixed penalty."
proposals.after: Moreover, it is just spring to carry out punishments. Allow me to itemize and memorialize the fixed penalty."
proposals.reason: 方春行刑 objects to punishment in spring rather than calling spring the execution season.

proposals.before: Fu again memorialized, "The late Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Jigao was public-spirited, loyal, and upright—a famous minister of the former court.
proposals.after: He again memorialized, "The late Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Jigao was public-spirited, loyal, and upright—a famous minister of the former court.
proposals.reason: In this Liu Hun narrative 復奏 means again memorialized, not the person Fu.

proposals.before: Fu again memorialized: 'The late Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Jigao was public-spirited, loyal, and upright—a famous minister of the former court.
proposals.after: He again memorialized: 'The late Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Jigao was public-spirited, loyal, and upright—a famous minister of the former court.
proposals.reason: 復奏 is again plus memorialized, not the name Fu.

proposals.before: In his oversight of the Secretariat, the chief clerk reported that he should call on officials. Hun said with a somber face, "Officials are arrayed with divided duties. If I further interfere, that is not ritual and law.
proposals.after: In his oversight of the Chancellery, the chief clerk reported that he should call on officials. Hun said with a somber face, "Officials are arrayed with divided duties. If I further interfere, that is not ritual and law.
proposals.reason: 判門下 is the Chancellery.

proposals.before: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying: With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids.
proposals.after: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying: 'With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids.'
proposals.reason: The literal English leaves Ma Sui's quoted congratulation unquoted, unlike the Chinese speech marks and the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist a enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway; yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said: 'Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony.'
proposals.after: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist an enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway; yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said: 'Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony.'
proposals.reason: The article before 'enlightened ruler' is ungrammatical ('a enlightened').

proposals.before: Feng Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;
proposals.after: Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;
proposals.reason: The Chinese names only 河清; the idiomatic surname Feng is not in the source and conflicts with the literal 'Heqing'.

decisions.reason: 轉祠部、右司二員外 records transfer to those two yuanwailang posts; it does not use 兼 or otherwise say they were held concurrently.

decisions.reason: The literal line likewise keeps 《》 around English titles instead of rendering 三禮圖, 五經微旨, and 孟子音義 as English book names.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 撰《三禮圖》九卷、《五經微旨》十四卷、《孟子音義》三卷

decisions.reason: After 杞乃偽請行 and 上固以不可, 因薦鎰 continues Lu Qi’s scheme: Qi, not the emperor, recommended Zhang Yi for the Fengxiang-Longyou posting.

decisions.reason: 鎰出鳳翔三十里，及二子皆為候騎所得 coordinates Zhang Yi with his two sons as those captured; 楚琳俱殺之 and the following 贈太子太傅 show he was killed too.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鎰出鳳翔三十里，及二子皆為候騎所得，楚琳俱殺之

decisions.reason: The literal likewise omits 鎰 from 及二子皆為候騎所得 and from 俱殺之; he and the two sons were jointly taken and killed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及二子皆為候騎所得，楚琳俱殺之

decisions.reason: 麟德 is the Linde reign, not Longde; 曾伯祖 is a paternal great-granduncle, not a great-great-uncle.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 麟德初為右相，祥道即從一曾伯祖也

decisions.reason: The literal repeats the same errors: 麟德 romanized as Longde and 曾伯祖 rendered as great-great-uncle.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 麟德初為右相，祥道即從一曾伯祖也

decisions.reason: 以親避除刑部員外郎 uses 除 as appoint; ‘removed and appointed’ invents a dismissal the Chinese does not state.
非鄙夫之心也 is ‘not the heart of a base/petty man’; rendering 鄙夫 as ‘honorable man’ inverts Fu’s refusal.
尚書郎 is a lang of the Shangshu (Department of State Affairs), not a Secretariat (中書) post.
The literal likewise mislabels 尚書郎 as a Secretariat directorship.
累除衢州司馬 is successive appointment; 除 here does not mean remove.
幾成老夫暗劣矣 predicates 暗劣 of the speaker as a dim, incompetent old man, not an abstract ‘old man’s incompetence.’
尚書左丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.
渾尚名載 means he was still named Zai; ‘name was still listed’ misses 名載 as the personal name 載.
The literal’s ‘name was still listed’ likewise fails 尚名載, ‘was still named Zai.’
判門下省 is oversight of the Chancellery, not the Secretariat.

decisions.after: Moreover, this would be carrying out punishment just in spring. Allow me to itemize and memorialize the fixed penalty."
decisions.reason: 方春行刑 objects to executing just as it is spring; the original treats spring as the execution season, but the proposed wording is still awkward and ambiguous.
In Liu Hun’s narrative 復奏 means he memorialized again; 復 is not the person Xiao Fu.
The literal also takes 復奏 as the name Fu; it is again plus memorialized, still Hun speaking.
其判門下 is his oversight of the Chancellery, not the Secretariat.
賀曰 introduces Ma Sui’s quoted congratulation, closed by 」; the literal leaves that speech unmarked.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 馬燧前賀曰：今之一盟，百年內更無蕃寇。」

decisions.reason: English requires ‘an enlightened ruler’; ‘a enlightened’ is ungrammatical and is not licensed by 明主.
The Chinese names only 河清; the surname Feng is not in this sentence and should not be supplied.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0026 shows Feng was supplied only by the bad idiomatic line; s0247 names 河清 alone, so the Feng Heqing name claim has no source.
